mh.opengrep.generic.secrets.security.det.reason: Matched the `"type": "service_account"` marker alone, so it reported form placeholders and documentation that show the shape of a key file (3 of 3 hits in TueriCXO, all UI placeholders). The marker is not a credential; the private key is. Replaced by mh.microhealth.generic.gcp-service-account-key, which requires the marker AND a private key with key material in the same file. A bare PEM private key is still caught by the private-key rules of both upstream sources and by Trivy.

Replaced by mh.microhealth.generic.jwt-token. This rule and gitleaks.jwt reported every token twice, and both reported the public Supabase ANON key (role=anon, shipped to every browser by design) in migrations that can never be edited (9 + 9 hits in TueriCXO, all anon keys). The replacement keeps the same token shape and exempts only a payload whose fixed claims are iss=supabase and role=anon; a service_role key or any other token is still reported.

mh.opengrep.javascript.lang.security.aud.reason: Its taint source is "any parameter of any function", so a helper called only with constant tag names was user input (22 hits in TueriCXO, all false). Replaced by mh.microhealth.javascript.regexp-from-untrusted-input (see above).

Reports any template literal passed as the first argument of console.* when more arguments follow (2,279 hits in TueriCXO, every one a console.log/warn/error). The harm it describes is that a `%s` inside the interpolated value makes console substitute a later argument into the line: the text of a log line changes, nothing executes, and the value was attacker-chosen log text already. Log injection proper (newlines, terminal escapes) is not what it detects either, so it carries no security signal and buried every real finding in the report.

mh.opengrep.javascript.lang.security.htm.reason: Reports every template literal that contains `<...>` and an interpolation: XML, SVG and PDF writers, LLM prompts, YAML comments, regex sources, CLI usage text. It ignores whether each value is escaped and whether the string is ever parsed as HTML (85 hits in TueriCXO, 84 false). Replaced by mh.microhealth.javascript.html-string-to-dom-sink, which follows interpolated values to the sinks that parse HTML (innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, srcdoc) and treats escaping helpers and DOMPurify as sanitisers; it finds the one real case (a document.write of unescaped vendor and model text).

mh.opengrep.javascript.lang.security.ins.reason: Its sink is every argument of Object.assign, including the TARGET, so writing a literal of fixed keys into a parsed object was "prototype pollution". Replaced by mh.microhealth.javascript.json-parse-into-object-assign: parsed JSON as a source argument, schema-validated values excluded.
